findings: Before the market change (steps 35 to 42), a transaction's own features were enough to catch 86% of illicit transactions at 72% precision (PR-AUC 0.89).

Network risk features did not help on this data: PR-AUC is 0.759 without them and 0.759 with the whole graph. They moved recall from 72% to 75% and precision from 57% to 39%. The benefit of sharing measured on synthetic data is not reproduced here.

From step 43, after a dark market closed, the model caught 0 of 169 illicit transactions. A model trained on the earlier period does not recognise what came after. This is the same weakness the synthetic "unseen pattern" test shows, now seen on real data.

notes: Real data, real labels, tested strictly on later time steps than it was trained on.
The features are anonymised by the publisher, so plain-language reason codes are not possible here.
This is Bitcoin, not UPI. It tests the method, not the Indian-payments model used in the live demonstration.
The three institutions are imaginary: each transaction is assigned to one by a hash of its ID.
A dark market closed around time step 43. The data set's authors report that the models they tested also lost most of their recall after that point.
Thresholds were chosen on only five time steps, so precision and recall at the threshold are noisy. PR-AUC does not depend on a threshold and is the fairer comparison between rows.
